newsitem.title: BELGIUM: 96 signals success ahead for Belgian UM.
newsitem.headline: 96 signals success ahead for Belgian UM.

text.p: Belgian metals firm Union Miniere will on Thursday report better figures for 1996, the last transition year for the company, as the first results of its restructuring show through, analysts said on Monday.

"In total I expect an improvement in the current results," KB-Securities analyst Michel Ernst said. "There will be the first positive signs from the restructuring. But 1997 could be Union Miniere's year. It could be fantastic."
Analysts said the heady combination of the rising dollar, higher zinc prices and lower interest rates should give a boost to the once lumbering company.

"I expect earnings per share of 61 francs against 51 francs in 1995," Ernst said. "It is clear that the second semester was sharply better than the first which was very difficult for Union Miniere and for other industrials."

"The improvement will come from the start of the rise in the dollar which began in the second semester of 1996, the start of the climb in zinc prices and also from the first signs of the restructuring plan coming through.
"I also expect a slight improvement in the financial results in 1996 from 1995 and I expect taxes to be limited," he added.
Analyst Loic De Caters of Generale Bank agreed.
"I expect somewhat better current earnings for 1996 from 1995," he said.
He put EPS in 1996 at 60 francs, in line with consensus estimates on Reuters Securities 3000.
"1996 was a transitional book year. Everyone expects much better figures in 1997 and even more in 1998 -- the final year of the restructuring plan initiated by Chief Executive Officer Karel Vinck."
The plan was put in operation in late 1995 and 1996 is seen as the bridging year before the first full effects are felt -- expected to be this year.
UM reported group net profits down 10 percent to 281 million francs in the first half of 1996.
In full year 1995 the firm, which specialises in non-ferrous metal production, recycling and building materials, had a net loss of 954 million francs but a current profit of 1.8 billion francs.
"I expect the net figure to be in the black, not much, but possibly enough to pay a dividend...of about 30 francs per share net," De Caters said.
Union Miniere last paid a dividend in book year 1990. It was 90 francs.
"A small dividend would be a positive message, perhaps symbolic, but important," De Caters said. "Union Miniere is financially very strong."
Analysts said that on the strength of the results they expected the UM share to continue its recent strong performance -- it has hugely outperformed both the market and the sector in the past year.
In the year to date the stock has risen 25 percent against the Bel-20's 15 percent climb and the non-ferrous metals sector's 10 percent rally.
At 1415 GMT it was up 20 francs at 2,710 francs. It hit a year high of 2,740 on March 6.
